jobs.title: Head of Customer Support
jobs.description:
About Cheaper Inference Cheaper Inference is a drop-in, OpenAI-compatible API that charges developers about 30% below provider list price
. We save money in two ways:
Marketplace pricing.
Providers with spare LLM capacity compete on price. We send each request to the cheapest healthy offer and pass the discount on to customers.
Fewer wasted tokens.
Our optimization pipeline uses current research to cut tokens from each request. Every customer can see exactly what each request saved.

Our customers are developers and technical teams running production workloads through our API. When something goes wrong, such as a failed request, a surprising bill or a confusing savings number, they need fast, accurate, technically credible help. Support is part of the product.

The role You'll build and lead customer support at Cheaper Inference from the ground up. You'll handle tickets yourself at first, then design the systems, tools, documentation and team that let support grow with the company. You'll be accountable for how fast we respond, how well we resolve issues, how satisfied customers are and how much of what you learn gets back to the product team.
You'll work closely with the founders and engineering. A large share of our support is technical. You'll often be the first to spot an API issue, a billing edge case or a confusing part of the dashboard.

What you'll do Own the support function.
Set up support channels (email, in-app chat, Discord or Slack communities), choose and configure the tools, and define SLAs, priority levels and escalation paths.
Handle tickets directly at first.
Answer technical questions about API integration, streaming, rate limits, errors, model availability, request headers, prompt A/B experiments and billing.
Run incident communication.
Work with engineering during outages or slowdowns. Post updates on the status page, let affected customers know proactively and follow up after incidents.
Build self-serve help.
Create and maintain help center articles, troubleshooting guides, FAQs and macros so customers can solve common problems themselves. Work with the docs team to fill gaps.
Handle billing and account issues.
Resolve questions about usage, invoices, credits, refunds, savings attribution and plan changes accurately and fairly.
Get customer feedback to the product team.
Tag and analyze tickets to find recurring problems, bugs and feature requests. Report clear, prioritized findings to product and engineering.
Use automation wisely.
Set up AI-assisted support (triage, suggested replies, a documentation chatbot) where it helps, without letting quality slip.
Hire and grow the team.
Decide when and who to hire, including support engineers and specialists. Build the onboarding, training and quality review processes they'll need.
Measure everything.
Track first response time, time to resolution, CSAT, ticket volume per customer and the share of issues customers solve on their own. Report on these regularly and keep improving them.
Support key accounts.
Work with sales and success on onboarding, migrations and dedicated support for high-value customers.

What success looks like First 90 days:
Support tools, SLAs and escalation paths in place. A core help center live. Response times and CSAT measured and improving. A regular report of customer feedback going to product.
First year:
A support operation that can grow, with a strong self-serve rate, consistently high CSAT, a clear plan for hiring the team and measurable product improvements driven by support findings.

What we're looking for 4+ years
in customer support or support engineering, including at least 1–2 years leading support or building it from scratch, ideally at an API, developer tool, infrastructure or SaaS company.
Strong technical skills. You're comfortable reading API docs, testing requests with curl or Postman, reading logs and error codes, and talking with engineers in their terms.
Experience with support platforms (e.g., Zendesk, Intercom, Plain, Front, Help Scout) and status page tools.
Excellent writing. Your replies are clear, empathetic and accurate, and your documentation actually gets used.
Experience handling billing and usage-based pricing questions.
Calm judgment during incidents and escalations.
A data-driven approach to support metrics and process improvement.
An owner's mindset and comfort doing the work yourself at an early-stage company.

Nice to have Experience with LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic or similar) or AI infrastructure products.
Basic scripting or SQL to investigate issues without waiting for engineering.
Experience running developer communities on Discord or Slack.
Experience setting up AI-assisted support workflows.

Why join Compensation: $100,000 - $135,000 + equity
You'll build a core function from scratch and shape how customers experience Cheaper Inference.
You'll work closely with the founders and engineering, where your input directly shapes the product.
You'll join a small, high-leverage team with real ownership.

jobs.title: Head of Supply Partnerships (Inference Providers)
jobs.description:
About Cheaper Inference Cheaper Inference is a drop-in, OpenAI-compatible API that charges developers about 30% below provider list price
. We help our customers save money in two ways:
Marketplace pricing.
Providers with spare LLM capacity compete on price. We send each request to the cheapest healthy offer and pass the discount on to customers.
Fewer wasted tokens.
Our optimization pipeline uses current research to cut tokens from each request. Every customer can see exactly what each request saved.

Our supply of inference capacity limits how far we can grow. The more good, reliable, low-cost capacity we have, the bigger the discount, the more models we can offer and the more customers we can serve.

The role You'll be the first person focused full-time on the supply side of the business. You'll find, sign, onboard and manage our relationships with inference providers. These include GPU clouds, model labs, resellers, enterprises with reserved capacity they don't use and neoclouds. You'll be accountable for how much capacity we have, what it costs, how reliable it is and how many models it covers.
You'll work closely with the founders and engineering. In this job, commercial deals and technical details go together: a good deal on a slow or unreliable endpoint is a bad deal.

What you'll do Build the supplier pipeline.
Find and rank providers with surplus or discountable capacity across models, regions and hardware. Run outreach from first contact to a live integration.
Negotiate and close.
Set pricing, volume commitments, rate limits, SLAs, payment terms and data-handling terms. Structure deals that keep us below list price while staying fair and sustainable for providers.
Onboard providers.
Work with engineering to connect new providers to our routing layer. Meet latency and throughput targets and report accurate usage.
Manage live relationships.
Track each provider's uptime, latency, error rates, fill rates and how competitive their prices are. Run regular business reviews, handle escalations and expand the relationships that work.
Protect supply resilience.
Avoid relying too heavily on one provider, keep backup capacity for our most popular models and plan ahead for demand spikes and new model launches.
Track the market.
Follow GPU and token pricing, new model releases, provider roadmaps and competitors. Turn what you learn into a supply strategy and pricing recommendations.
Own trust and compliance with partners.
Make sure providers meet our standards for data retention, privacy, security (e.g., SOC 2) and acceptable use. Work with legal on contracts and DPAs.
Shape the marketplace.
Help design incentives, pricing mechanics and provider-facing tools and processes that attract and keep good capacity.

What success looks like First 90 days:
A mapped list of target providers, at least 3–5 new providers signed and live, and a clear view of the health of current supply.
First year:
A deep, diverse provider base covering all major models, measurable gains in price and reliability, and a repeatable process for bringing on new providers.

What we're looking for 4+ years
in partnerships, business development, supply or procurement, ideally at an AI infrastructure company, cloud or GPU provider, or a two-sided marketplace.
An existing network across inference providers, GPU clouds or model labs, or a clear plan for building one fast.
A strong commercial sense. You're comfortable with unit economics, margin, usage-based pricing and capacity commitments.
Enough technical depth to discuss tokens per second, time to first token, rate limits, quantization, context windows and API compatibility with engineers on both sides.
A track record of negotiating and closing complex contracts.
Comfort with data. You can build the dashboards and models you need to manage supply (SQL or spreadsheets).
An owner's mindset and comfort with ambiguity at an early-stage company.

Nice to have Experience with open-weight model serving (vLLM, TGI, SGLang) or GPU capacity markets.
A background in marketplace design, trading or commodity procurement.
Familiarity with enterprise security and compliance reviews.

Why join Compensation: $150,000 - $250,000 + equity
You'll own a function that directly sets our product's price, quality and growth.
You'll work at the center of a fast-moving market for AI compute.
You'll join a small, high-leverage team with real ownership.

The Vice President, Financial Accounting & Reporting is a senior accounting and controllership executive for a global public company. Working in close partnership with the CFO, the VP, Financial Accounting & Reporting ensures the integrity, discipline, and operational effectiveness of the company’s financial management framework across accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, audit oversight, compliance, and revenue accounting globally.

Partner with risk management and internal audit.
Support the CFO in Audit Committee matters and serve as a senior operational counterpart on financial governance, controls, and compliance topics.
Ensure accounting processes scale effectively as the business grows in complexity across geographies, products, commercial models, and regulatory obligations.
Grow high-performing teams and create an environment that supports collaboration, operational excellence, and modern enterprise thinking.

What we are looking for

15 years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Significant experience with public-company reporting, external audit, internal controls,

regulatory compliance, and Audit Committee support.

TSX experience is required; NASDAQ and NYSE experience is highly desirable.
Deep knowledge of IFRS, US GAAP, SOX, and internal control frameworks is highly

desirable, including direct experience owning SOX/ICFR programs.

Strong understanding of revenue recognition (IFRS 15/ASC 606) and operational finance

best practices.

Big Four public accounting background, particularly with public-company audit, SEC/OSC
reporting, SOX/ICFR, or complex technology clients.
An active CPA designation is required for this role.
Strong presentation and communication skills at the senior management and board level

Our platform directly helps companies power the world’s supply chains. We see the results of what we do out in the world every day, when we see store shelves stocked, when medications are available for our loved ones, and so much more.

Companies across industries trust us to help them take control of their integrated business planning and digital supply chain. Some of our customers include Lockheed Martin, Unilever, P&G, ExxonMobil, Cisco and more.

We are seeking an experienced Nuclear Project Director to support the growth and delivery of complex nuclear and energy capital projects across Canada and North America. This role will provide senior leadership across strategic project portfolios, major project execution, client engagement, governance, risk management, and multidisciplinary delivery. The successful candidate will bring a proven ability to lead large capital programs from proposal, early planning through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness.

This is a senior, delivery and client-facing leadership role for a professional who can quickly assess business priorities, establish project discipline, build strong delivery teams, and support clients through complex decisions involving capital allocation, operational risk, reliability, safety, stakeholder expectations, and long-term asset performance.

Engineering degree or related technical qualification is preferred; graduate education in project management, business administration, or a related discipline is an asset.
Professional licensure or eligibility preferred (P.Eng. + PMP).
15-18 years of experience in the nuclear, energy, or related sector, including business development, project management, and technical leadership for major infrastructure.
Extensive senior leadership experience in project direction, project portfolio management, capital project execution, operations leadership, and general management within energy, nuclear, aerospace, or related sectors.
Demonstrated experience leading major capital projects and portfolios, including projects valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars.

Track record of improving project outcomes through value engineering, contractor engagement, cost optimization, project controls, and disciplined issue resolution.
Experience supporting nuclear or energy sector clients through strategic growth, operational improvement, reliability, maintenance, and asset performance initiatives.
Strong executive presence and ability to work effectively with senior leadership teams, Boards of Directors, clients, contractors, government stakeholders, and community partners.
Experience working with Indigenous communities and an understanding of the importance of respectful engagement, partnership, social license, and community benefit in major project development.
Ability to build, motivate, and lead high-performing teams over multi-year project lifecycles.
Proven experience in nuclear business development in a market-facing role is required.

Have a degree/diploma or combined relevant work experience and certifications (8-10 years) in Information Systems, law or policy management.

Security certifications such as CISM, CISA, and CRISC.
Experience with implementing an Information Security Management System (ISMS) and ISO 27001 certification a benefit
Strong understanding of technology risk regulatory, and industry best practice (ISO 27000 Series, NIST, PCI)
Proven ability to identify, analyze and translate risk in the context of what it means to achieving business objectives

Sound and practical business minded approach to implementation of a GRC program.
Experienced in the ability to influence and guide others across the organization to solve challenging problems.
Experience with leading GRC platforms, technologies and solutions is an asset
Build and foster strong relationships through collaboration, influencing change, and building consensus
You bring your real self to work and you live our values – trust, teamwork, open communication and accountability.

Ability to acquire secret clearance

holds a key position responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining a robust compliance program to ensure that CDS Clearing and Depository Services Inc. (CDS) and the Canadian Derivatives Clearing Corporation (CDCC) each operate within their applicable legal and regulatory frameworks. This mandate covers the complete end-to-end compliance framework for both entities.

The CCO ensures an integrated compliance strategy by coordinating with the Businesses, Risk Management, Internal Audit and Enterprise Compliance functions, as well as with the TMX General Counsel’s Office. Providing assurance on the effectiveness of post-trade compliance, the CCO reports directly to the Board of Directors and the Vice President, Regulatory Affairs and Enterprise Compliance.

Given that CDS and CDCC are recognized clearing agencies and designated systemically important Financial Market Infrastructures (FMIs), the CCO is tasked with ensuring strict adherence to applicable legal and regulatory requirements, including those stemming from such federal designation and provincial recognitions. In this role, the CCO also liaises directly with key regulators.

Work Location:
We are open to candidates being located in one of the following Canadian office locations: Toronto or Montreal.

Key Accountabilities

Compliance Strategy & Oversight
Ensure the continued development of a strong, credible, robust culture of compliance through leading the function with excellence, practicality, and strong relationships with the businesses, risk management, legal, TMX affiliates, and external stakeholders
Assess the overall compliance framework for CDS and CDCC and adapt it to the evolution of the post-trade businesses and their regulatory requirements, accounting for the systemically important nature of these businesses and their similarities and differences; and on an ongoing basis, reassess the compliance framework to ensure it continues to be fit for purpose
Serve as a strategic advisor on the compliance impact of changes to post-trade businesses, including changes to rules, risk frameworks and IT infrastructure
Maintain and oversee written policies, procedures and controls to ensure compliance with applicable federal and provincial laws, regulations (including National Instruments), Recognition Orders, and Oversight Agreements and international obligations (collectively the Regulatory Requirements), and monitor regulatory and industry trends affecting the FMIs
Ensure timely and appropriate review of written policies and procedures is undertaken regarding the operation of the clearing agencies, develop and conduct training and monitoring to ensure policies and procedures are understood and complied with
Collaborate with the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) to ensure that compliance risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated within each FMI's overall enterprise risk management framework

Meet, as appropriate, with staff at the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) and the Bank of Canada (BoC) to discuss compliance matters, coordinate with the General Counsel’s Office and other stakeholders to respond to questions from relevant regulators and maintain relationships with such regulators

Prepare and certify an Annual Compliance Report assessing the overall health of the compliance programs, including the FMIs’ compliance with regulatory requirements for submission to the Board and regulators

Meet in camera with the Board and/or designated committees, as needed, and at least once annually to discuss the state of the compliance program

Monitor and report any breaches of regulatory requirements to applicable stakeholders on a timely basis
Respond promptly and assist as needed in incident management or crisis scenarios, coordinating with risk management, legal, business, operations, technology and other internal stakeholders in the execution of post-trade controls, surveillance, incident management and reporting
Collaborate with business lines to periodically update recovery and wind-down plans, which ensure systemic stability by detailing how FMIs manage severe stress, allocates uncovered losses, or safely winds down operations, and participate in default management and recovery plan simulations

Experience: Minimum 10 years of compliance experience within a regulated entity, including at least 3 years in a primary compliance leadership role
Regulatory Engagement/Oversight: Proven experience liaising directly with capital markets, banking, or other regulators (e.g., Bank of Canada, CSA, OSFI), and developing and executing compliance frameworks in a complex regulatory environment
Industry Knowledge: Deep expertise in compliance requirements for regulated entities, such as financial market infrastructures or financial institutions

Nice to Have(s)

Language Skills: Professional proficiency in French is an asset

About GHD | Energy Business

GHD’s Energy business is positioned for significant growth across the Americas, with priority areas including power generation, transmission and distribution, battery energy storage systems, hydropower, future fuels, gas-to-power, renewable natural gas, carbon capture, and major project delivery for mining and industrial clients. We bring together advisory, engineering, environmental, permitting, Indigenous engagement, project management, and delivery expertise to support clients across the full project lifecycle.

Our Hybrid Model:
Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in the office three days a week to contribute, connect, and excel in our vibrant environment.

Location:
Ontario (Waterloo, Toronto, Mississauga, Markham, Whitby, Peterborough, St. Catherines)

Who are we looking for?

We are seeking an experienced Nuclear Project Director to support the growth and delivery of complex nuclear and energy capital projects across Canada and North America. This role will provide senior leadership across strategic project portfolios, major project execution, client engagement, governance, risk management, and multidisciplinary delivery. The successful candidate will bring a proven ability to lead large capital programs from proposal, early planning through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness.

This is a senior, delivery and client-facing leadership role for a professional who can quickly assess business priorities, establish project discipline, build strong delivery teams, and support clients through complex decisions involving capital allocation, operational risk, reliability, safety, stakeholder expectations, and long-term asset performance.

Working with an energetic and high-performing team, this position will see you involved in:

Serve as Project Director on complex nuclear, energy, and major infrastructure and advisory projects, providing senior oversight from concept and feasibility through execution, commissioning, and closeout.
Lead strategic project portfolios, including capital planning, project selection, governance, prioritization, and execution readiness for clients with large-scale CAPEX programs.
Support GHD’s Energy growth objectives by helping originate, shape, and deliver opportunities across nuclear power, nuclear waste, nuclear decommissioning, renewable power generation, hydropower, transmission and distribution, and industrial energy systems.
Partner with Market and Sector Leaders, Business Group Leaders, Relationship Managers, technical specialists, and regional delivery teams to develop capture plans, position GHD for strategic pursuits, and convert opportunities into profitable backlog.
Provide executive-level client leadership, building trusted relationships with nuclear operators, OEMs, waste management, Indigenous communities, government agencies, contraction partners, and financing organizations.
Lead multidisciplinary project teams, including engineering, environmental, permitting, Indigenous engagement, project controls, procurement, construction management, commissioning, and operations readiness resources.
Establish and implement project governance, risk management, change management, commercial controls, communication protocols, and decision-making frameworks that improve delivery certainty.
Drive safety leadership and promote a strong site safety culture across project teams, contractors, and client stakeholders.
Guide value engineering, constructability reviews, scope control, cost optimization, schedule recovery, and issue resolution on major capital projects.
Mentor project managers and emerging leaders, strengthening GHD’s project delivery capability and helping build a scalable major projects platform across Energy.
Collaborate across Canada, the United States, and global GHD networks to leverage technical capability, Global Collaboration Centres, and best-practice delivery models.

What you will bring to the team:

Engineering degree or related technical qualification is preferred; graduate education in project management, business administration, or a related discipline is an asset.
Professional licensure or eligibility preferred (P.Eng. + PMP).
15-18 years of experience in the nuclear, energy, or related sector, including business development, project management, and technical leadership for major infrastructure.
Extensive senior leadership experience in project direction, project portfolio management, capital project execution, operations leadership, and general management within energy, nuclear, aerospace, or related sectors.
Demonstrated experience leading major capital projects and portfolios, including projects valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars.
Proven ability to lead end-to-end project execution, including facility design, equipment selection, consultant and contractor selection, construction management, commissioning, and operations turnover.
Strong commercial acumen, with experience managing scope, cost, schedule, procurement, contracts, risk, change, and governance on complex projects.
Track record of improving project outcomes through value engineering, contractor engagement, cost optimization, project controls, and disciplined issue resolution.
Experience supporting nuclear or energy sector clients through strategic growth, operational improvement, reliability, maintenance, and asset performance initiatives.
Strong executive presence and ability to work effectively with senior leadership teams, Boards of Directors, clients, contractors, government stakeholders, and community partners.
Experience working with Indigenous communities and an understanding of the importance of respectful engagement, partnership, social license, and community benefit in major project development.
Ability to build, motivate, and lead high-performing teams over multi-year project lifecycles.
Proven experience in nuclear business development in a market-facing role is required.
Commitment to health, safety, quality, inclusion, collaboration, and GHD’s values as an employee-owned organization.
Experience with Design Bid Build (DBB), Design Build (DB), and alternative delivery projects such as Progressive DB, Integrated Project Delivery/Alliance and/or P3 considered an asset.

Working in close partnership with the CFO, the VP, Financial Accounting & Reporting ensures the integrity, discipline, and operational effectiveness of the company’s financial management framework across accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, audit oversight, compliance, and revenue accounting globally.

Support the CFO in Audit Committee matters and serve as a senior operational counterpart on financial governance, controls, and compliance topics.
Ensure accounting processes scale effectively as the business grows in complexity across geographies, products, commercial models, and regulatory obligations.
Grow high-performing teams and create an environment that supports collaboration, operational excellence, and modern enterprise thinking.

15 years of progressive financial leadership experience.
Significant experience with public-company reporting, external audit, internal controls,

regulatory compliance, and Audit Committee support.

TSX experience is required; NASDAQ and NYSE experience is highly desirable.
Deep knowledge of IFRS, US GAAP, SOX, and internal control frameworks is highly

desirable, including direct experience owning SOX/ICFR programs.

Strong understanding of revenue recognition (IFRS 15/ASC 606) and operational finance

best practices.

Big Four public accounting background, particularly with public-company audit, SEC/OSC

Strong presentation and communication skills at the senior management and board level

Job Description

About GHD | Energy Business

GHD’s Energy business is positioned for significant growth across the Americas, with priority areas including power generation, transmission and distribution, battery energy storage systems, hydropower, future fuels, gas-to-power, renewable natural gas, carbon capture, and major project delivery for mining and industrial clients. We bring together advisory, engineering, environmental, permitting, Indigenous engagement, project management, and delivery expertise to support clients across the full project lifecycle.

Our Hybrid Model:
Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in the office three days a week to contribute, connect, and excel in our vibrant environment.

Location:
Ontario (Waterloo, Toronto, Mississauga, Markham, Whitby, Peterborough, St. Catherines)

Who are we looking for?

We are seeking an experienced Nuclear Project Director to support the growth and delivery of complex nuclear and energy capital projects across Canada and North America. This role will provide senior leadership across strategic project portfolios, major project execution, client engagement, governance, risk management, and multidisciplinary delivery. The successful candidate will bring a proven ability to lead large capital programs from proposal, early planning through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness.

This is a senior, delivery and client-facing leadership role for a professional who can quickly assess business priorities, establish project discipline, build strong delivery teams, and support clients through complex decisions involving capital allocation, operational risk, reliability, safety, stakeholder expectations, and long-term asset performance.

Working with an energetic and high-performing team, this position will see you involved in:

Serve as Project Director on complex nuclear, energy, and major infrastructure and advisory projects, providing senior oversight from concept and feasibility through execution, commissioning, and closeout.
Lead strategic project portfolios, including capital planning, project selection, governance, prioritization, and execution readiness for clients with large-scale CAPEX programs.
Support GHD’s Energy growth objectives by helping originate, shape, and deliver opportunities across nuclear power, nuclear waste, nuclear decommissioning, renewable power generation, hydropower, transmission and distribution, and industrial energy systems.
Partner with Market and Sector Leaders, Business Group Leaders, Relationship Managers, technical specialists, and regional delivery teams to develop capture plans, position GHD for strategic pursuits, and convert opportunities into profitable backlog.
Provide executive-level client leadership, building trusted relationships with nuclear operators, OEMs, waste management, Indigenous communities, government agencies, contraction partners, and financing organizations.
Lead multidisciplinary project teams, including engineering, environmental, permitting, Indigenous engagement, project controls, procurement, construction management, commissioning, and operations readiness resources.
Establish and implement project governance, risk management, change management, commercial controls, communication protocols, and decision-making frameworks that improve delivery certainty.
Drive safety leadership and promote a strong site safety culture across project teams, contractors, and client stakeholders.
Guide value engineering, constructability reviews, scope control, cost optimization, schedule recovery, and issue resolution on major capital projects.
Mentor project managers and emerging leaders, strengthening GHD’s project delivery capability and helping build a scalable major projects platform across Energy.
Collaborate across Canada, the United States, and global GHD networks to leverage technical capability, Global Collaboration Centres, and best-practice delivery models.

What you will bring to the team:

Engineering degree or related technical qualification is preferred; graduate education in project management, business administration, or a related discipline is an asset.
Professional licensure or eligibility preferred (P.Eng. + PMP).
15-18 years of experience in the nuclear, energy, or related sector, including business development, project management, and technical leadership for major infrastructure.
Extensive senior leadership experience in project direction, project portfolio management, capital project execution, operations leadership, and general management within energy, nuclear, aerospace, or related sectors.
Demonstrated experience leading major capital projects and portfolios, including projects valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars.
Proven ability to lead end-to-end project execution, including facility design, equipment selection, consultant and contractor selection, construction management, commissioning, and operations turnover.
Strong commercial acumen, with experience managing scope, cost, schedule, procurement, contracts, risk, change, and governance on complex projects.
Track record of improving project outcomes through value engineering, contractor engagement, cost optimization, project controls, and disciplined issue resolution.
Experience supporting nuclear or energy sector clients through strategic growth, operational improvement, reliability, maintenance, and asset performance initiatives.
Strong executive presence and ability to work effectively with senior leadership teams, Boards of Directors, clients, contractors, government stakeholders, and community partners.
Experience working with Indigenous communities and an understanding of the importance of respectful engagement, partnership, social license, and community benefit in major project development.
Ability to build, motivate, and lead high-performing teams over multi-year project lifecycles.
Proven experience in nuclear business development in a market-facing role is required.
Commitment to health, safety, quality, inclusion, collaboration, and GHD’s values as an employee-owned organization.
Experience with Design Bid Build (DBB), Design Build (DB), and alternative delivery projects such as Progressive DB, Integrated Project Delivery/Alliance and/or P3 considered an asset.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Every transaction matters. Every Canadian matters. At Interac, we protect both — driving trust, security, and inclusion, so our digital economy thrives.

Founded in 1984, Interac connects Canadians through secure digital payments, advanced identity verification and industry-leading fraud protection. Connecting banks, businesses, and individuals, Interac enables millions to send, receive, and manage money safely and effortlessly every day — across both digital and physical environments.

As the backbone of Canada’s financial ecosystem, Interac facilitates over 20 million transactions daily, supported by trusted partnerships with government and financial institutions. Consistently ranked as Canada’s most reputable financial technology brand, Interac is deeply embedded in the daily lives of Canadians.

Who You Will Work With:

Leader, Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) will be responsible for establishing the GRC mandate and goals for Interac Corp. and will collaborate closely with key stakeholders and business units on security risk and compliance initiatives and effective risk management practices across the organization. The Leader, will business units embed a security risk management culture into production, delivery, support and operations that enables business objectives.

The Leader will be responsible for strengthening controls in IT environments, ensuring that risks are clearly understood, controls are implemented to mitigate those risks and continuous monitoring is established to measure control effectiveness.

The Leader, will lead a team in operating and maintaining an Information Security Management System (ISMS) to help Interac Corp. meet and comply with applicable frameworks, data protection laws, regulations, Interac cybersecurity standards and contractual obligations.

What You Will Do:

Review corporate policies, identify additional policies and develop policies to enhance existing controls and alignment with ISO 27000 series, NIST and PCI standards and frameworks.
Socialize policies and standards and provide guidance to employees on adherence to the policies.
Coordinate and guide the Information Security Risk Management process risk owners to ensure that risk treatments are effective.
Support the internal IT audit function and external auditors and established organizational security certifications.
Assist in the development, training and tracking of the internal control environment associated with the various standards (e.g. SOC 2, ISO27001/2).
Conduct compliance activities to ensure adherence with relevant policies, standards, regulations, and applicable laws
Manage internal auditors and external auditors and activities.
Regularly update and review risk portfolio for changes in the environment. Provide regular reporting of significant risks and the risk portfolio to pertinent Management Committees.
Drive improvements in the organization arising from the identification of risk and control gaps that balance risk with business operations.
Act as a key point of contact when identifying risk to raise awareness with security management and business unit leads on a risk reduction plan.
Maintain a registry of risk remediation supported by a governance lifecycle and the implementation of management tools that are technology enabled.

new_jobs.description:
Venture outside the ordinary - TMX Careers

The TMX group of companies includes leading global exchanges such as the Toronto Stock Exchange, Montreal Exchange, and numerous innovative organizations enhancing capital markets. United as a global team, we’re connecting cross-functionally, traversing industries and geographies, moving opportunity into action, advancing global economic growth, and propelling progress. Through a rich exchange of ideas, meaningful collaboration, and a nimble operating model, we're powering some of the nation's most critical systems, fueling capital formation and innovation, bringing increased opportunity to business visionaries, product ingenuity to consumers, and career exploration to our team.

Ready to be part of the action?

The Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)
holds a key position responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining a robust compliance program to ensure that CDS Clearing and Depository Services Inc. (CDS) and the Canadian Derivatives Clearing Corporation (CDCC) each operate within their applicable legal and regulatory frameworks. This mandate covers the complete end-to-end compliance framework for both entities.

The CCO ensures an integrated compliance strategy by coordinating with the Businesses, Risk Management, Internal Audit and Enterprise Compliance functions, as well as with the TMX General Counsel’s Office. Providing assurance on the effectiveness of post-trade compliance, the CCO reports directly to the Board of Directors and the Vice President, Regulatory Affairs and Enterprise Compliance.

Given that CDS and CDCC are recognized clearing agencies and designated systemically important Financial Market Infrastructures (FMIs), the CCO is tasked with ensuring strict adherence to applicable legal and regulatory requirements, including those stemming from such federal designation and provincial recognitions. In this role, the CCO also liaises directly with key regulators.

Work Location:
We are open to candidates being located in one of the following Canadian office locations: Toronto or Montreal.

Key Accountabilities

Compliance Strategy & Oversight
Ensure the continued development of a strong, credible, robust culture of compliance through leading the function with excellence, practicality, and strong relationships with the businesses, risk management, legal, TMX affiliates, and external stakeholders
Assess the overall compliance framework for CDS and CDCC and adapt it to the evolution of the post-trade businesses and their regulatory requirements, accounting for the systemically important nature of these businesses and their similarities and differences; and on an ongoing basis, reassess the compliance framework to ensure it continues to be fit for purpose
Serve as a strategic advisor on the compliance impact of changes to post-trade businesses, including changes to rules, risk frameworks and IT infrastructure
Maintain and oversee written policies, procedures and controls to ensure compliance with applicable federal and provincial laws, regulations (including National Instruments), Recognition Orders, and Oversight Agreements and international obligations (collectively the Regulatory Requirements), and monitor regulatory and industry trends affecting the FMIs
Ensure timely and appropriate review of written policies and procedures is undertaken regarding the operation of the clearing agencies, develop and conduct training and monitoring to ensure policies and procedures are understood and complied with
Collaborate with the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) to ensure that compliance risks are identified, assessed, and mitigated within each FMI's overall enterprise risk management framework
Lead the management and delivery of annual disclosures against international standards designed to ensure the safety, efficiency, and resilience of clearing, payment, and settlement systems (i.e., the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (PFMI)), including ensuring that appropriate senior clearing agency staff are identified to "own" each key consideration of an applicable PFMI principle, that each owner understands and applies the required PFMI assessment methodology, and periodically assessing the PFMI compliance program including by benchmarking against global peers
Meet, as appropriate, with staff at the Canadian Securities Administrators (CSA) and the Bank of Canada (BoC) to discuss compliance matters, coordinate with the General Counsel’s Office and other stakeholders to respond to questions from relevant regulators and maintain relationships with such regulators
Act as a trusted advisor on compliance matters to CDS and CDCC, including responding to early warning questions, establishing trust and open communication with the businesses to allow for proactive detection and remediation; and advise business lines on compliance regarding Participants’ and Clearing Members’ adherence to rules, procedures and manuals
Coordinate responses to due diligence questionnaires from Participants covering a variety of areas, including AML, KYC, politically exposed persons, cyber security
Governance & Board Reporting
Prepare and certify an Annual Compliance Report assessing the overall health of the compliance programs, including the FMIs’ compliance with regulatory requirements for submission to the Board and regulators
Engage with the relevant Boards as needed regarding, apprising the Board of material non-compliance that poses a risk to market participants or the broader financial system
Meet in camera with the Board and/or designated committees, as needed, and at least once annually to discuss the state of the compliance program
Incident/Crisis Management
Monitor and report any breaches of regulatory requirements to applicable stakeholders on a timely basis
Respond promptly and assist as needed in incident management or crisis scenarios, coordinating with risk management, legal, business, operations, technology and other internal stakeholders in the execution of post-trade controls, surveillance, incident management and reporting
Collaborate with business lines to periodically update recovery and wind-down plans, which ensure systemic stability by detailing how FMIs manage severe stress, allocates uncovered losses, or safely winds down operations, and participate in default management and recovery plan simulations

Must Have(s)

Experience: Minimum 10 years of compliance experience within a regulated entity, including at least 3 years in a primary compliance leadership role
Regulatory Engagement/Oversight: Proven experience liaising directly with capital markets, banking, or other regulators (e.g., Bank of Canada, CSA, OSFI), and developing and executing compliance frameworks in a complex regulatory environment
Industry Knowledge: Deep expertise in compliance requirements for regulated entities, such as financial market infrastructures or financial institutions
Leadership & Collaboration: Track record of driving strong compliance culture, and collaborating effectively across legal, enterprise risk, operations, business and finance functions
Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the proven ability to communicate effectively to all levels in an organization, including C-suite executives and Boards of Directors

Nice to Have(s)

Domain Expertise: Specialized experience and strong operational familiarity with Canadian securities, derivatives, clearing, and settlement systems
Language Skills: Professional proficiency in French is an asset

The recruiting efforts for this role are intended to fill a vacant position.

In the market for…

Excitement
- Explore emerging technology and innovation, as well as ventures and digital finance that shape the future of global markets! Experience the movement of the market while grounded in the stability of close to 200 years of success.

Connection
- With site hubs in some of the world’s most multicultural cities, we leverage our size and structure to create rich connections and belonging while experiencing powerful global impact through our work.

Impact
- More than a platform, we use our talents to power mission-critical systems that drive global economic advancement, innovation, and growth. As well, our employee-led Team Impact spreads social good via our giving strategy.

Wellness
- From empathetic leadership to a culture of flexibility and balance, we believe wellness at work creates the maximum yield and a stronger “we”. Plus, with a cloud-first and hybrid workstyle, as well as generous time-off and leaves, we support a life well lived!

Growth
- From a growth mindset in our work, to expansion in our business, TMX is home to action-takers energized by the achievement of ambitious growth.

Ready to enrich your career with impactful work, leaders who truly care, and the flexibility and programs to help you thrive as part of #TeamTMX ? Apply now.

Job Description

About GHD | Energy Business

GHD’s Energy business is positioned for significant growth across the Americas, with priority areas including power generation, transmission and distribution, battery energy storage systems, hydropower, future fuels, gas-to-power, renewable natural gas, carbon capture, and major project delivery for mining and industrial clients. We bring together advisory, engineering, environmental, permitting, Indigenous engagement, project management, and delivery expertise to support clients across the full project lifecycle.

Our Hybrid Model:
Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in the office three days a week to contribute, connect, and excel in our vibrant environment.

Location:
Ontario (Waterloo, Toronto, Mississauga, Markham, Whitby, Peterborough, St. Catherines)

Who are we looking for?

We are seeking an experienced Nuclear Project Director to support the growth and delivery of complex nuclear and energy capital projects across Canada and North America. This role will provide senior leadership across strategic project portfolios, major project execution, client engagement, governance, risk management, and multidisciplinary delivery. The successful candidate will bring a proven ability to lead large capital programs from proposal, early planning through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness.

This is a senior, delivery and client-facing leadership role for a professional who can quickly assess business priorities, establish project discipline, build strong delivery teams, and support clients through complex decisions involving capital allocation, operational risk, reliability, safety, stakeholder expectations, and long-term asset performance.

Working with an energetic and high-performing team, this position will see you involved in:

Serve as Project Director on complex nuclear, energy, and major infrastructure and advisory projects, providing senior oversight from concept and feasibility through execution, commissioning, and closeout.
Lead strategic project portfolios, including capital planning, project selection, governance, prioritization, and execution readiness for clients with large-scale CAPEX programs.
Support GHD’s Energy growth objectives by helping originate, shape, and deliver opportunities across nuclear power, nuclear waste, nuclear decommissioning, renewable power generation, hydropower, transmission and distribution, and industrial energy systems.
Partner with Market and Sector Leaders, Business Group Leaders, Relationship Managers, technical specialists, and regional delivery teams to develop capture plans, position GHD for strategic pursuits, and convert opportunities into profitable backlog.
Provide executive-level client leadership, building trusted relationships with nuclear operators, OEMs, waste management, Indigenous communities, government agencies, contraction partners, and financing organizations.
Lead multidisciplinary project teams, including engineering, environmental, permitting, Indigenous engagement, project controls, procurement, construction management, commissioning, and operations readiness resources.
Establish and implement project governance, risk management, change management, commercial controls, communication protocols, and decision-making frameworks that improve delivery certainty.
Drive safety leadership and promote a strong site safety culture across project teams, contractors, and client stakeholders.
Guide value engineering, constructability reviews, scope control, cost optimization, schedule recovery, and issue resolution on major capital projects.
Mentor project managers and emerging leaders, strengthening GHD’s project delivery capability and helping build a scalable major projects platform across Energy.
Collaborate across Canada, the United States, and global GHD networks to leverage technical capability, Global Collaboration Centres, and best-practice delivery models.

What you will bring to the team:

Engineering degree or related technical qualification is preferred; graduate education in project management, business administration, or a related discipline is an asset.
Professional licensure or eligibility preferred (P.Eng. + PMP).
15-18 years of experience in the nuclear, energy, or related sector, including business development, project management, and technical leadership for major infrastructure.
Extensive senior leadership experience in project direction, project portfolio management, capital project execution, operations leadership, and general management within energy, nuclear, aerospace, or related sectors.
Demonstrated experience leading major capital projects and portfolios, including projects valued in the hundreds of millions of dollars.
Proven ability to lead end-to-end project execution, including facility design, equipment selection, consultant and contractor selection, construction management, commissioning, and operations turnover.
Strong commercial acumen, with experience managing scope, cost, schedule, procurement, contracts, risk, change, and governance on complex projects.
Track record of improving project outcomes through value engineering, contractor engagement, cost optimization, project controls, and disciplined issue resolution.
Experience supporting nuclear or energy sector clients through strategic growth, operational improvement, reliability, maintenance, and asset performance initiatives.
Strong executive presence and ability to work effectively with senior leadership teams, Boards of Directors, clients, contractors, government stakeholders, and community partners.
Experience working with Indigenous communities and an understanding of the importance of respectful engagement, partnership, social license, and community benefit in major project development.
Ability to build, motivate, and lead high-performing teams over multi-year project lifecycles.
Proven experience in nuclear business development in a market-facing role is required.
Commitment to health, safety, quality, inclusion, collaboration, and GHD’s values as an employee-owned organization.
Experience with Design Bid Build (DBB), Design Build (DB), and alternative delivery projects such as Progressive DB, Integrated Project Delivery/Alliance and/or P3 considered an asset.
